item.description: Texas Longhorns Athletic Director Chris Del Conte looks at a replay during the game against the Mississippi Rebelsin the second half at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin on Saturday Oct. 24, 2026. (Jay Janner/Austin American-Statesman) The Big 12 needs a new commissioner, but Texas Longhorns athletic director Chris Del Conte insists that it won't be him. On Wednesday, Del Conte said that he wasn't interested in leading the Big 12 Conference. According to On Texas Football, there was speculation that the Big 12 wanted to court either Del Conte or American Conference leader Tim Pernetti as its next commissioner. "Absolutely none," Del Conte told On Texas Football when asked if he had interest in the job. Del Conte then told the publication to "print that." Rumor that the Big 12 is courting Chris Del Conte or Tim Pernetti as its next commissioner. Was told this morning CDC has no interest in that job. "Absolutely none," CDC said. "Print that." #HookEm - Bobby Burton (@BobbyBurtonOTF) November 11, 2026 The Big 12 will soon need to replace Brett Yormark, who is stepping away after nearly five years on the job. Texas was in the Big 12 when Yormark was hired. Del Conte has been at Texas since December 2017. Under his watch, the Longhorns have won five Directors' Cup , claimed 18 national championships, made a slew of successful coaching hires and smoothly transitioned into life in the SEC. Before Texas, the 58-year-old Del Conte led the athletic departments at TCU and Rice. Due to a contract extension that Del Conte signed in 2025, he is set to make $3 million during the 2026-27 fiscal year . He is guaranteed a raise during every year of a contact that ends in 2036. item.title: Who will call plays for Oregon after Mehringer's firing?
item.description: EUGENE — After firing first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer seven games into the 2026 season, Dan Lanning shared Oregon ’s plans for filling his role moving forward at his weekly press conference Monday night. Offensive assistant Jay Johnson will lead offensive playcalling for the Ducks going forward, Lanning said. “He has a lot of experience as a play-caller, was with me in Georgia when we were part of the national championship team,” Lanning said. “Went on to have a lot of success in Colorado and Michigan State. He’s gonna lead the efforts there with the offensive staff, but it’ll still be a collaborative effort, with a lot of the work that we do. “He’s also coming in with a different perspective, a different view, not being with us the last few years, where he can provide a couple things that might be different than what we’ve done.” Mehringer, previously the tight ends coach for the Ducks, is the first assistant coach Lanning has fired in his tenure at Oregon, which began in 2022. The Ducks’ offensive decision-making was at the center of intense criticism over the past three weeks, during which Oregon averaged just 14 points per game and lost twice to UCLA and Illinois. Lanning spoke to the human element of letting Mehringer go. “They see the football coach, right? That’s also an unbelievable dad. A great husband,” Lanning said. “The guy’s been part of our staff for the last five years, that’s done some really good things here, and I think all of us feel like we shoulder some of the blame. item.title: Lanning: Stewart incident 'didn't match our standard'
item.description: EUGENE — After Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was booked in Springfield Municipal Jail early Sunday morning on DUII charges, Ducks coach Dan Lanning addressed the situation at his weekly press conference Monday. “There was an incident this weekend that didn’t match our standard here in our program,” Lanning said. “There will be an appropriate action taken. Still gathering some details with what that situation looks like. But that would be handled internally. I’m not gonna respond to any other questions about that. We’re gonna handle that with our guys. “There’s an expectation of what you have to... how you have to act, and how you need to perform in our program. Kind of overshadows the success that we had on Saturday, which is disappointing, but that will be handled by us internally. I’m not going to speak on it publicly.” When Lanning was asked a follow-up question about a rumored speeding incident involving other Oregon football players, for which there haven’t been any confirmed arrests, he said, “I was talking about the same thing when I first addressed it.” This is also the second instance of an Oregon football team member facing DUII charges in the past year. In April, running backs coach Ra’Shaad Samples allegedly backed his Ford F-150 into a parked car outside a bar in Eugene. His next court date is Oct. 27. An arraignment for Stewart in his DUII case hasn’t been set, as official charges haven’t been filed to Springfield Municipal Court as of Monday evening, according to court records. Stewart leads the Ducks this season with 27 catches for 352 yards and four touchdowns. He missed Saturday’s win over Nebraska due to an undisclosed injury. Oregon (4-2, 2-1 Big Ten) is preparing for a road game at Illinois (3-3, 1-2) at 12 p.m. PT this coming Saturday. item.description: A first-round home game is one thing. Winning it in the CIF State playoffs? That's another. Because at this point in the season, there are no easy opponents . The field is filled with some of California's best girls volleyball programs, and the difference between seeds doesn't always tell the whole story. Four San Joaquin County teams had the opportunity to begin their state championship journeys at home Tuesday, Nov. 10. And despite the level of competition, all four made the most of it. Here's how each team fared in the opening round of the CIF State girls volleyball playoffs, along with the scores and a full recap. Division II No. 1 St. Mary's 3, No. 16 Cardinal Newman 2 Earning the No. 1 seed comes with expectations. For a program with five Northern California championships, 14 Sac-Joaquin Section titles and 32 league championships, St. Mary's knows those expectations well. But against Cardinal Newman, the North Bay-Oak League champion, living up to them took everything the Rams had. St. Mary's came from behind to secure a dramatic 19-25, 25-16, 25-17, 22-25, 15-13 victory. A team that finished the regular season with 80 consecutive TCAL wins suddenly found itself in unfamiliar territory, trailing 11-9 and later 13-12 in the deciding set. For a closer look at how St. Mary's survived, read The Record's full game story. Division III No. 3 Ripon 3, No. 14 Washington 0 For five straight years, Ripon has reached a section championship game. And for five straight years, that has earned the Indians a spot in the state tournament. But until Tuesday, one thing had been missing. A state tournament victory. Ripon finally checked that box with a 25-21, 25-21, 25-10 sweep of San Francisco's Washington, which entered 23-8 after placing third in the Academic Athletic Association at 11-3. The Indians, ranked No. 70 in California by MaxPreps compared with Washington's No. 233 ranking, got another strong performance from junior outside hitter Ashlyn Malone, who followed her 18-kill section championship outing with 12 kills, six digs and two aces. Freshman outside hitter Lilia Tuputala added 11 kills, senior opposite Jorie Eskes had nine, and senior setter Alayna Sprinkle finished with 27 assists and 10 digs after recording 41 assists in the section final. Senior libero Kennedy Everhart anchored the defense with 23 digs. item.title: 76ers' Jaylen Brown Addresses Icy Pregame Interaction With Celtics' Jayson Tatum
item.description: 76ers' Jaylen Brown Addresses Icy Pregame Interaction With Celtics' Jayson Tatum originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jaylen Brown insisted he had no beef — but maybe some "lamb chops" — with former teammate Jayson Tatum. An icy interaction between the two before tipoff on Tuesday might have said otherwise, but once basketball became the focus, the two kept it professional. Tatum and Brown played the game without incident, but one of them decisively had the better night. Tatum and the Celtics rolled to a 123-101 win, with Brown struggling as the 76ers fell behind. After the game, Brown took the high road and explained the awkward pregame interaction with his former Celtics co-star. Here's a look at what Brown had to say. Jaylen Brown discusses Jayson Tatum faceoff Brown told reporters after the loss that he "wasn't paying attention" when Tatum approached him and put his arms around him moments before tipoff. "I'm just focused on doing what's best for my team," Brown said. "Everything else is just... to be honest, I wasn't paying attention." On a night in which he struggled mightily, Brown gave credit to his former teammate by name. "Credit to Jayson. He played well tonight," Brown said. "Credit to the Celtics." Jaylen Brown postgame on the foul trouble that affected his night, what he was feeling coming into the night, and his response when asked about the pre-tip moment with Jayson Tatum. https://t.co/XNSRuWmRSv — Chris Hine (@ChristopherHine) November 11, 2026 Tatum wasn't the focal point for the Celtics, as his 21 points on 8-of-17 from the field paled in comparison to Paul George's 36-point outburst, but he did play better than Brown. The 76ers star didn't reach double-digit points until late in the fourth quarter, scoring 13 points on 4-of-9 from the field and finishing a team-worst minus-27. After the loss, Brown admitted he was "frustrated" with his performance. "I wanted to perform better for my team," Brown said. "Foul trouble kind of derailed me a little bit, but you know, it happens." Joel Embiid, LeBron James and VJ Edgecombe all struggled offensively as well, so the loss certainly wasn't all on Brown. But the contrast between Brown's tough night and George's outstanding performance was stark after the two were traded for each other in the summer. item.title: UAlbany women's basketball off to hot start under Morrone, but tough opponents await
item.description: UAlbany head coach Kelly Morrone talks to the media after beating Manhattan on Thursday, Nov. 5, at the Broadview Center in Albany, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) Kelly Morrone has five pillars that define what her University at Albany women's basketball program is all about: Character, connection, trust, a "never back down" mentality and an unbreakable spirit. "This week," Morrone said, "is testing that unbreakable spirit pillar." The Great Danes are off to a 3-0 start in Morrone's first season at the helm, but things are about to get a whole lot tougher. UAlbany flew south Tuesday to play a top-25 Ole Miss team in a 7 p.m. contest Wednesday at The Sandy and John Black Pavilion in Oxford, Miss., and the team will follow that up Monday by traveling to Piscataway, N.J. to face Rutgers. Two games in less than a week against teams from the SEC and Big 10 are certain to test the Great Danes. "You see games like this, and you see some of the scores around the country," Morrone said. "Every team wants to compete. What do you do when all of a sudden you feel overwhelmed by size or speed? You just can't back down. You've got to keep your spirit up and understand that it's a great opportunity to grow as an individual player, as a position group, or as a team in general." "There's lots of different ways to win in these games," she added. Against Ole Miss, UAlbany will face a team that's ranked 21st in the latest AP poll and 24th in the coaches' poll. The Rebels have won their first two games by an average of 31.5 points. The Great Danes, on the other hand, started their season by pulling out close wins over Northeastern and Manhattan by a combined five points before a more comfortable 77-57 win Sunday on the road against Mount St. Mary's. "We had eight quick turnovers (on Sunday) that kind of smacked us in the face," Morrone said. "But, once we settled in and really started making some shots and doing a great job of defensive rebounding and using the whole floor, it was really nice to see the ball go through the hoop and to get a bit of a lead and know how to keep it." Morrone praised the strong play from forward Madison Roman, who followed the Great Danes' coach from her previous job at Merrimack, and freshman Alexia Bujold. Sophomore Emma Zuccon, one of the team's two returning players from 2025-26, played a huge role in Sunday's win, scoring 13 points and grabbing seven rebounds in 14 minutes while Roman battled foul trouble. item.title: Paul George Delivers His Loudest Celtics Statement In Return To Philadelphia
item.description: Paul George Delivers His Loudest Celtics Statement In Return To Philadelphia originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Paul George could hardly have scripted a more satisfying return to Philadelphia. The Boston Celtics forward scored 36 points Tuesday night, helping his new team defeat the 76ers 123-101 in a game loaded with storylines surrounding the summer trade that sent Jaylen Brown in the opposite direction. George made six 3-pointers and finished 14-for-28 from the field. He was particularly effective when Boston needed separation, turning what could have been an emotional distraction into an impressive individual performance. The victory also gave the Celtics their ninth win in 10 games. MORE: Celtics Fans Noticed an Unbelievable Detail in Jayson Tatum's Dunk on LeBron James George Takes Control Of An Emotional Night Most of the attention entering Tuesday centered on Jayson Tatum facing Brown for the first time in a regular-season game. George, however, became the central figure once the ball was tipped. His ability to score from the perimeter and create shots gave Philadelphia problems throughout the evening. The veteran forward also delivered a powerful fourth-quarter stretch as Boston pulled away. His six successful attempts from beyond the arc accounted for 18 points, reinforcing how much spacing he provides alongside Tatum. The Celtics made 22 3-pointers as a team, repeatedly punishing Philadelphia for defensive breakdowns. Boston Gets An Early Return On Its Gamble Trading Brown was one of the most consequential decisions in recent Celtics history. George's age and contract made the transaction controversial, even with additional draft compensation coming to Boston. Tuesday offered a reminder that George remains capable of producing at an elite level when his shooting and offensive rhythm align. Tatum contributed 21 points, while Payton Pritchard added 18. Boston's balanced supporting production made it difficult for Philadelphia to concentrate its defense on either star. Brown finished with 13 points for the 76ers, giving the first regular-season meeting an especially striking contrast. One November game cannot settle the long-term debate over the trade. George nevertheless delivered exactly the kind of performance Boston envisioned when it reshaped its roster, and he did it in the arena where the decision carried the most personal significance. item.title: Jordan Scott Owned the Paint Against Duke
item.description: No. 5 Michigan State upset No. 2 Duke 79-73 on Tuesday night at the Champions Classic at the United Center in Chicago. The Spartans won it on the defensive end, and sophomore Jordan Scott had as much to do with that as anyone on the floor. Michigan State blocked eight Duke shots, and Scott had six of them. Cam Ward, the Spartans big man who came off the bench to score 14 points, did not need much prompting to say what Scott does for this defense. “Jordan is the X factor on defense,” Ward said, per ESPN . “He does it all. He had six blocks tonight. He’s everywhere all the time, and it’s just a luxury to have him on our team, especially when he can be that guy for us.” Detroit Free Press beat reporter Chris Solari posted the line from the postgame room. Nov 10, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Michigan State Spartans forward Jordan Scott (6) defends Duke Blue Devils guard Cayden Boozer (2) during the first half at United Center. Mandatory Credit: David Banks-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Tom Izzo Said Jordan Scott Changed the Game Tom Izzo got to the same place from the other direction. Scott shot 2-for-7 from the floor and 1-for-4 from 3-point range, and his head coach still called it about as good a game as a player can have on that kind of shooting night. “Not impressive, and yet he probably changed the whole game himself with his defense, with his rebounding, with his effort-related stats,” Izzo said, per the Detroit Free Press . Jordan Scott Is Michigan State’s Rim Protector Scott is averaging 2.7 blocks and 1.7 steals through three games, and the Duke night carried most of it. Cam Ward Came Off the Bench and Contributed Ward was a factor off the bench for the Spartans too. He scored 14 points on 5-for-7 shooting, went 4-for-4 at the free-throw line, grabbed six rebounds and blocked a shot in 20 minutes. He has not started a game this season and is averaging 7.7 points. It is important for Michigan State to get as many contributions as possible for this team to be successful. Nights like Tuesday are a reason the Spartans are off to a 3-0 start.

(Jay Janner/Austin American-Statesman) Texas football would qualify for the College Football Playoff if the regular season ended before this weekend's slate of games. But the Longhorns' spot in the college football's postseason tournament still isn't secure with three games remaining. On Tuesday, Texas was ranked the No. 6 team in the latest CFP rankings. The Longhorns won the game 17-27. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) Steve Sarkisian 's team dropped two games in October to unranked opponents in Oklahoma and Florida . The defeats make Texas one of six two-loss teams in the current 12-team playoff field, a number that will likely grow in the coming weeks. Ten two-loss teams have qualified for the College Football Playoff across the last two years. Its rare to see a three-loss playoff team, however, with the only two exceptions (Clemson in 2024 and Alabama in 2025) being teams that played in their conference championship game. GOLDEN : Longhorns shows they can win a tough road game - and a whole lot more FILM STUDY : Arch Manning made this winning move vs. Mizzou Texas is safe for now. But will a third loss this season knock Sarkisian and Co. out of the the Playoff? >And what games should Texas fans be on the lookout for this week? Texas has simple route to CFP qualification Let's not complicate matters. Win each of the next three games, and Texas is effectively guaranteed CFP inclusion. The Longhorns' seeding would then be the biggest question, one with multiple potential answers. Texas could close the regular season with wins over LSU, Arkansas and Texas A&M and still miss the SEC championship, then reach the CFP as a 10-2 at-large selection. Being an at-large team likely mean Texas would host a first-round game or hit the road for one. UT would, of course, qualify for the CFP if it did make and win the SEC championship, a scenario in which the Longhorns would then likely receive a top-four seed and subsequent first-round bye. Would Texas be in jeopardy of missing the playoff if it won the next three games, then lost the SEC championship? Unlikely. Alabama's CFP inclusion last year provides the proper precedent. Lose your third game in the conference title game, and you won't incur a penalty. For Texas, the formula remains simple: win the next three games, and the championship chase will stay alive, regardless of the conference result. item.title: Tuchel warns England against arrogance as Croatia seek revenge for 7-0 humiliation
item.description: Tuchel warns England against arrogance as Croatia seek revenge for 7-0 humiliation Thomas Tuchel has warned England not to underestimate Croatia following a 'freak' 7-0 win over this week's opponents last month. England welcome Croatia to Wembley on Thursday night in the UEFA Nations League . The fixture is the reverse match from last month's clash in Rijeka, when England produced arguably their best performance of Tuchel's reign. Harry Kane and Bukayo Saka each scored twice in a 7-0 win for the Three Lions , who became the first team to score five or more goals in an away fixture against Croatia. Morgan Rogers, Anthony Gordon and Jude Bellingham were also on target. The win was a statement result from England and leaves them in contention to top the group. However, Tuchel has warned his squad not to underestimate Croatia in the return, insisting their seven-goal win was a 'one-off'. Tuchel warns England not to underestimate Croatia: 7-0 win was a “freak, a one-Off” "It was a deserved result, but it was a freak, a one-off. It did not reflect the quality and strength of the Croatia national team and they showed a reaction very quickly and they could have won the [next] game against Spain but conceded a late goal," he said at his pre-match press conference. "Croatia is a proud country and a country full of quality. They want to show that it was a one-off and for us it is important to forget this result and not chase the same result. We have to match the intensity and be stronger in the intensity than the opponent and show up with the right intensity and right attitude to be able to win this match. "This match matters to us 100%. We want to win this match to have a chance to win the group in Spain, that's where our focus is. We expect a reaction from Croatia and we have to start with the same humbleness and show up with a top team performance. "In football anything can happen. A result like this should not give us one per cent of arrogance or over-confidence, why would it? We should be courageous and self-confident enough to admit it was a deserved result, but big teams respond and Croatia are a big team, they have shown this in many tournaments. "We start from scratch, we start from 0-0. Croatia is a technical team, an emotional team, that's what Croatia represents, individual players who are proud to play for the country. I expect a reaction and don't expect a result like in the first match."

item.title: Deion Sanders Stands Firm On Offensive Coordinator Amid Struggles
item.description: Joe Camporeale-Imagn Images Deion Sanders will not fire offensive coordinator Brennan Marion, even as Colorado’s offense sputters through a 3-6 season. The head coach told reporters on Tuesday that he has full confidence in his staff while admitting the team’s scoring formula simply does not work right now. Fans in Boulder do not want changes., but Sanders insists the solution lies in adjustments rather than replacements. The Buffaloes need to win their final three games to reach a bowl, starting with a tough Friday night game against Houston. Sanders Defends His Play-Caller Pressure mounts after a 20-10 loss to Arizona State left Colorado with little margin for error. When asked directly if he considered handing play-calling duties to someone else, Sanders gave a firm, one-word answer: “No.” Yet he acknowledged that conversations are happening behind closed doors regarding potential tweaks. He made it clear that while he respects Marion, the current results are unacceptable. “I’m not happy with the outcome,” Sanders told reporters after the game. Colorado averaged only 19.8 points per game, ranking last in the Big 12 and in the nation’s bottom 15. Before arriving in Boulder, Marion’s offenses averaged more than 30 points per game over six seasons. Sanders had built his program’s identity around that 30-point benchmark, noting that the team went 13-3 when hitting that mark in his first three years. This season, the Buffs have reached that score only once, during a blowout win over FCS opponent Weber State. Shared Blame on Both Sides Sanders refuses to pin the entire failure on his offense. When questioned if averaging 30 points would have fixed their record, he pointed to defensive lapses. “We gave up points as well,” he said. “I walked into the room, I put in how many points we score a game and how many we give up. And I’m saying this don’t work,” he explained. The team has held opponents to 29 points or fewer but has dropped four conference games, and offensive stalls have prevented defensive stops from securing victory. Despite the criticism, Sanders maintains he loves his staff and respects them deeply. “I love Brennan. I respect the heck out of them,” Sanders said. He emphasized that any changes would not be malicious but necessary. “Some things we may just have to do a little different.” He also shut down rumors about his own job security, stating he is focused on the players. “Man, I don’t think about that, man. I’m not here for my job. I’m here for these young men,” Sanders said. Recruiting and Roster Challenges The staff will deal with challenges beyond this season as the team loses key recruits. Three-star tackle Li’Marcus Jones recently flipped to Mississippi State, marking the third decommitment since late October. Jones had originally committed in May, but he chose to go home and play in the SEC instead. This trend follows similar moves by linebacker Jahmiere Portis-Daniels and wide receiver Ryan Ferdinand, who flipped to Cincinnati.

item.title: Are the Washington Commanders still suffering a Week 5 hangover?
item.description: Dan Quinn | Getty Images The New York Giants face the Washington Commanders on Thursday, the second and final meeting of the season between the two NFC East teams. We turn to Andrew York of Hogs Haven to answer our ‘5 questions’. Ed: How have the Commanders moved on from the dysfunctional way that the Week 5 game against the Giants ended? Is there still a hangover from that? Andrew: It’s funny, because the Giants fumbled away a chance at the win in overtime when they could have made a field goal to win, yet all the media scrutiny seemed to be on the Commanders… However, I’d agree that the decision making around the very last play drew lots of justified criticism on both the Commanders coaching and Jayden Daniels for not having better situational awareness. It was followed up with a similar end-of-game play against the 49ers the very next week that drew criticism of both the coaches and Jayden Daniels. I think that double whammy got people looking at everything a bit more closely, but it’s really just been a litany of questionable decisions (mostly with the coaching and offensive playcalling) over multiple games that has Commanders fans unhappy with their play on the field. Most of the scrutiny has been on OC David Blough, who skipped a few grade levels going from Assistant QB Coach to OC when maybe he needed more time to learn his craft. I honestly put that more on Dan Quinn for promoting him too quickly though, I wouldn’t expect anyone to do well with that big of a promotion. Ed: Jameis Winston was the Giants’ quarterback in Week 5. Now, it will be J.J. McCarthy. Does that change anything for the Commanders? Andrew: From a gameplanning standpoint, sure, mainly in that McCarthy is a mobile QB and the defense will have to account for his scrambles. McCarthy also seems to have done a better job throwing deep this year. However, those are just things they’ll have to account for in the gameplan. I don’t think it provides more of a challenge over QBs like Brock Purdy that they’ve already faced. His mobility might be the biggest challenge, as the Commanders allowed Jalen Hurts to scramble for 46 yards earlier this year, getting several critical first downs. Ed: Can Dan Quinn possibly keep his job if this turns into a four- or five-win season for the Commanders? Andrew: I don’t think so. The biggest problem for the Commanders seems to be coaching, with the most yards erased by penalty in the NFL, slow playcalls and players taking too much time to get into position, and regular mistakes in situational awareness and game management that lose games. The defense has looked better coached the last few games with the addition of Steve Wilks as a defensive consultant , but it speaks very poorly of Dan Quinn (a supposedly defensive head coach) that he had to bring in an external defensive consultant to improve the defense mid-season. item.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
item.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. item.title: Damian Lillard is back and Ja Morant is here. How exactly is this going to work? | Bill Oram
item.description: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone’s list. Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always. Morant doesn’t particularly address any of those, and yet, he’s here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. It’s happening. “It’s easy for people to be like, ‘Man how is this going to work,’” Lillard offered. “‘They can’t do this, they can’t do that.’ But being on the floor with them … we can be a dangerous team and I really believe that.” The onus is on the Trail Blazers starting this month to prove that they bet right in acquiring Morant. And that pairing him with Lillard isn’t the boondoggle conventional wisdom suggests it will be. Lillard noted how many teams that succeeded in the playoffs last year, think San Antonio with its four point guards, relied on numerous playmakers. To his credit, Morant said he would be comfortable coming off the bench, if necessary. But they would not be the first NBA team to fall into the trap of believing they are capable of adjusting or that they will be comfortable sacrificing. It isn’t uncommon to see players in those situations default to familiar habits and sensibilities once the season is underway or struggles come. That’s what made a lot of the positive energy around what sure seems like an awkward roster ring so hollow. We’re going to need to see it to believe it. item.title: Ciryl Gane Reveals How Jon Jones Defeat Changed His Mindset as a UFC Fighter
item.description: Jon Jones beats Ciryl Gane for the heavyweight title at UFC 285 | Photo: @ufcespanol/YouTube | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Kshitiz Kumar Singh Ciryl Gane is preparing for his first heavyweight title defense against Josh Hokit in the main event of UFC 334. The Frenchman was recently elevated to undisputed champion after Tom Aspinall vacated the title due to further complications with his eye injury. However, much of the attention surrounding the Madison Square Garden headliner has focused on Gane’s legitimacy as champion and the growing criticism of his illegal tactics inside the Octagon. While the Frenchman has pushed back against accusations of being a dirty fighter, he recently made another revealing admission ahead of his showdown. Gane opened up about his defeat to Jon Jones at UFC 285 , describing the experience as a major turning point in his career. The reigning champion also reflected on how the loss affected his confidence and changed his mindset as a fighter. Ciryl Gane Explains How His UFC 285 Loss to Jon Jones Fueled His Comeback At UFC 285 in March 2023, Jones made his long-awaited heavyweight debut after nearly four years away from competition. He challenged Gane for the vacant heavyweight championship, with the Frenchman entering the contest fresh off a knockout victory over Tai Tuivasa at UFC Paris. Many expected Gane to provide Jones with a difficult test, considering the latter was moving up a division and returning after an extended layoff. However, the fight unfolded very differently. Despite taking an early groin strike, Jones quickly took control of the contest, secured a takedown and locked in a guillotine choke. Gane was forced to tap in less than three minutes, handing Jones his second UFC championship. Speaking in a recent interview with UFC on Paramount+ , Gane reflected on the defeat and said, “I think it was after the Jon Jones loss because it was a real loss.” Although Gane had already suffered his first professional MMA defeat against Francis Ngannou at UFC 270, that fight went the distance, with the Cameroonian winning by unanimous decision. The loss to Jones, however, was a much more decisive setback. Gane explained, “The fight against Francis Ngannou was a little bit square, but after Jon Jones, something changed in my mindset because also the pressure of social media from everywhere.” The 36-year-old further opened up about the criticism he received and the doubts he had about continuing his career. He added, “Like, ‘Ciryl Gane, we overestimated him,’ blah, blah, blah. I was disappointed. It was 2023, and I started MMA in 2019, so I already did pretty much in four years. One side of my head was about to give my back to everyone, but because I’m a competitor and because I want to prove to myself, I’m going to stay. I’m going to prove to myself.'” Since that setback, Gane has remained unbeaten, defeating Alexander Volkov at UFC 310 before earning another heavyweight title opportunity against Aspinall at UFC 321
